Conjugacy means prior times likelihood has the same distributional family as the prior. Beta–Bernoulli updates add successes/failures; Dirichlet–categorical updates add category counts; a Gamma(shape, rate) prior with Poisson counts adds total counts to shape and total exposure to rate. Gaussian observations with known variance add precision and precision-weighted observations to a Gaussian prior. [1](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book1.html)

For a scalar observation with fixed-dimensional sufficient statistics, these updates can be constant time per event and need no MCMC. The blanket $O(1)$ claim is false when dimension grows: storing a K-category posterior takes $O(K)$ space, and multivariate Gaussian covariance updates involve matrix operations. Conjugacy gives analytical tractability, not dimension-free computation. The posterior is exact only under the selected likelihood/prior assumptions, which still require validation.
